evidence: Selecting API module filtered list to 5 API documents (API Versioning Strategy, Error Handling Standards, HTTP Methods Guide, Rate Limiting, REST API Design Guidelines); clicking All restored full list of 19 documents.

Selecting 'REST API Design Guidelines' displayed title, description, date (2024-01-15), version (v2.3.0), Content Sections (REST Principles, Endpoint Naming Conventions, Pagination & Filtering), and Related Documents (API Versioning Strategy, Error Handling Standards, HTTP Methods Guide, Rate Limiting).
Clicking 'API Versioning Strategy' in Related Documents of REST API Design Guidelines navigated the document view to show API Versioning Strategy as the active document.

Clicking 'Versioning Approaches' section header collapsed it: body paragraph disappeared, and reference link changed to a non-interactive chip 'REST API Guidelines' (no cursor=pointer), while the section header remained clickable to reopen.
Re-clicking 'Versioning Approaches' header restored the body paragraph and the reference link 'REST API Guidelines' became clickable (cursor=pointer) again.
Section header chevron icon has class 'rotate-180' when expanded (body/links visible) and no rotate class when collapsed (body/links hidden), giving a clear, state-consistent indicator.

Clicking the 'REST API Guidelines' reference chip while its section was collapsed kept the current document open and showed toast 'Please expand the section to access links'. After expanding the section, clicking the same link navigated to REST API Design Guidelines.

Observed 'REST API Design Guidelines' document: its content-section references (API Versioning Strategy, Error Handling Standards, HTTP Methods Guide) and Related Documents list (API Versioning Strategy, Error Handling Standards, HTTP Methods Guide, Rate Limiting) do not include itself. Same holds for 'API Versioning Strategy' (references REST API Guidelines, Error Handling; related docs list REST API Design Guidelines, Error Handling Standards) - no self-reference.

Clicking node 'REST API Design Guidelines' gave it a pulsing glow ring and thicker stroke (stroke-width 3 vs 2 for unselected) as selection indication. Zoom In raised 100%->120%->140%, Zoom Out reduced back, and Reset View returned display to 100%, all shown in the on-screen zoom percentage indicator.

Graph renders 19 nodes matching the 19 documents seen in the 'All' document list across all 5 modules (API, Authentication, Data Layer, UI Components, Core System) shown in the legend, with 19 connection lines drawn between related documents. Reset View control brings the full graph back to 100% zoom/default pan so the complete graph is visible.

Graph contains exactly 19 nodes (one per available document), each colored by its module per the Modules legend (API, Authentication, Data Layer, UI Components, Core System), and 19 lines connect related documents (e.g., REST API Design Guidelines connects to API Versioning Strategy, Error Handling Standards, HTTP Methods Guide, Rate Limiting).

issue: Graph node click does not open Document View
actual: Clicking a document node in the Knowledge Graph (e.g. 'Database Schema Design', 'OAuth 2.0 Integration') only visually selects the node (adds glow/thicker stroke) and remains on the Knowledge Graph tab; the nav bar 'Knowledge Graph' stays active. The selected document is only shown after the user manually clicks the 'Documents' tab. This requires a separate tab change, contrary to the expected behavior of opening the document view directly.

evidence: On 'Database Schema Design', collapsed 'Naming Conventions' and expanded 'Indexing Strategy', then set graph zoom to 140%. After switching Documents -> Knowledge Graph -> Favorites -> Documents -> Knowledge Graph, the selected document, per-section expand/collapse states, and the 140% zoom level were all retained exactly.

Navigation bar exposes three buttons: Documents, Knowledge Graph, Favorites. Clicking each one switches main content to the corresponding view (document list/detail, interactive graph, favorites list) and marks the button active.

issue: Favorites view does not expose all favorited documents when a Documents module filter is active
actual: Favorited 'Accessibility Standards' (UI Components) and 'API Key Management' (Core System) - nav badge correctly showed 'Favorites 2' and both markers ('Remove from favorites') survived changing sort order to 'Last Updated' and survived a full page reload (persistence confirmed working). However, after applying the 'API' module filter in the Documents tab and then switching to the Favorites tab, the Favorites view displayed 'No favorites yet' instead of the 2 favorited documents, because the module filter from Documents carried over and neither favorite belongs to the API module. Clearing the filter back to 'All' in Documents was required before Favorites would show its items again. This violates the requirement that the Favorites view continue to expose every favorited document regardless of a module filter used in Documents.

evidence: Typing a non-matching search term 'zzznonexistentquery123' into the document search box replaced the document list with a clear 'No documents found' message and helper text 'Try adjusting your search or filter criteria'. Clearing the search box restored the full 19-document list immediately.
